provenance.reportBaseline: Selected build interactions reference the supplied 7.42 report. Its Dota2ProTracker examples are from 7.41f.
provenance.method: The pick notes and purchase paths are curated for the indicated roles. Prices and observed matchup outcomes come from separate sources.

plans.pickNote: A flexible carry when your team already has a way to hold one target. Check illusion and save picks before committing to an Omnislash-centered fight plan.
watchFor: Saves or disarms can waste a damage window

goodAgainst.note: If your team isolates Drow, reaching melee range threatens her positioning and lets Omnislash concentrate on her.

avoidAgainst.note: Phantom Lancer copies can absorb Omnislash hits and hide the real target.
Naga illusions can split slashes. Clear copies and isolate a target first.

bad.note: Buy a cheap fighting item and a farming tool before saving for a large upgrade.

good.note: Use Phase and Maelstrom to farm and reach fights, then add Yasha movement and attack speed.

easy.note: Finish Mjollnir while the map is open, then work toward Scepter to unlock the 75%-potency attacks during Blade Fury.

swaps.note: Prioritize finishing the lightning upgrade against a persistent wall of copies.

bridge.note: Use Maelstrom for affordable wave and illusion clear. Finish Mjollnir later if the copies are still the main problem.

swaps.note: If allies also deal physical damage, apply Corruption before the team’s burst.
Pick up Pierce before luxury damage when the target is dodging attacks.
Bring early health-restoration reduction when repeated attacks can keep the debuff active.
Use the dispel against silences and other dispellable effects that stop your follow-up.

plans.pickNote: Choose Chaos Knight when Reality Rift can expose one enemy to Phantasm and opposing area clear is manageable.

goodAgainst.note: Rift threatens a back-line Zeus if you can close the distance and reach him with the copies.

avoidAgainst.note: Sven cleave can hit multiple Phantasms grouped around the Rift target.
A tightly clustered Phantasm group can give Earthshaker more Echo Slam targets.

bad.note: Fight around Armlet and the cheap Orb rather than committing straight to a large luxury item.

good.note: Armlet plus Diffusal lets Phantasm apply mana burn at full Item Potency.

easy.note: Buy early Blink to convert farm into initiations, then add Shard for follow-up pressure.

swaps.note: Protect the real hero against repeated nonpiercing control before spending more on initiation.
Time allied physical burst around Corruption. Phantasms apply its full-strength debuff and repeat applications refresh it.
Add a cheap anti-heal option that can be refreshed by eligible illusions.
Pierce also works on illusions in 7.42, with separate illusion proc damage.

plans.pickNote: Good in extended melee fights against high-health targets or ordinary magic control. Draft an ally who can get you onto slippery targets.
watchFor: Limited wave clear before a farming item

goodAgainst.note: Feast likes high-health frontliners, but respect the threat of Dismember and enemy follow-up.

avoidAgainst.note: Repeated disengage makes the fight depend on ally catch.

bad.note: Keep the first fight timing low with Phase and Armlet, then buy cheap stickiness and anti-heal.

good.note: Armlet and Yasha keep damage and movement online while you build toward lockdown.

easy.note: Buy Radiance first when lanes and camps are safe. Add Armlet next and consider the later Sabatons slot upgrade.

swaps.note: Prioritize keeping a target in melee once you can reach it.
Add Pierce when misses prevent both damage and sustain.
Pressure Ghost Scepter or other dispellable defensive buffs. In 7.42 Nullify also reduces allied forced movement on the target.

plans.pickNote: Pick Sven when enemies must stand together or rely on copies and summons. Line up a second initiator if fights start at long range.

goodAgainst.note: Great Cleave helps thin Phantom Lancer copies when their formation is tight.
Cleave punishes clustered Phantasms.

bad.note: Use a cheap attack-speed item and Crystalys for farm and an early fight window.

good.note: Echo Sabre adds an early hit spike. Blink lets you choose the target and approach angle.

easy.note: Finish Harpoon while ahead to close the last gap, then buy damage and spell protection.

swaps.note: Buy debuff immunity before optional damage if disables are consuming God's Strength.
Choose an armor swing that also supports allied physical damage and tower pressure.
Start next to the target when ranged positioning is the obstacle.
Get Pierce before critical damage if evasion is blocking the kill.

plans.pickNote: Prefer Phantom Assassin against exposed back-line targets that cannot easily punish your jump. Wait for enemy lockdown and evasion answers to be revealed.

goodAgainst.note: Can reach Zeus from a favorable angle if his team lacks instant counter-initiation.

avoidAgainst.note: Berserker's Call punishes a predictable jump, so wait for Axe to commit first.
Duel threatens an exposed entry, especially if Legion has Blink and follow-up.

bad.note: Skip the farming detour if your team needs immediate damage. Group around early Desolator and allied control.

good.note: Build Battle Fury on an open map, then buy spell protection before overcommitting in fights.

easy.note: Convert an early Battle Fury timing to a fast Desolator and take towers after clean kills.

swaps.note: Move BKB before the damage spike when disablers can reliably lock the first jump.
Buy a direct evasion answer when repeated misses block kills.
Bring a dispel for Ghost Scepter and other dispellable saves once you have enough damage to punish the target.

plans.pickNote: Flexible tempo mid with a way to enter and leave side-lane fights. Make sure another teammate supplies reliable lockdown.
watchFor: Enemies who can survive the first burst

goodAgainst.note: Blink gives you an angle onto a Drow who wants to maintain range.
Can approach Sniper from outside the normal front-to-back line if his team lacks instant lockdown.

avoidAgainst.note: Instant Hex threatens a predictable Blink entry. Wait for Lion to show or spend it.

bad.note: Invest in repeatable farming and poke before saving for your defensive item.

good.note: Use Orchid to turn Blink into pickoffs while enemy dispels are still scarce.

easy.note: Use the extra gold for a durable spell-damage build, then push toward Scepter.

swaps.note: Bring BKB forward when nonpiercing instant control threatens the first Blink.
Disable the save hero before committing the team’s burst.
If the team lacks a Vessel buyer, take the early anti-heal timing.

plans.pickNote: Pick Viper for a lane or frontline matchup where ranged pressure and Viper Strike Break matter. Draft someone who can catch mobile enemies.
watchFor: Enemy ability to play away from Viper

goodAgainst.note: Time Viper Strike's Break for the allied burst window against Bristleback.
Break can suppress a breakable defensive passive during the kill attempt.

avoidAgainst.note: Storm can bypass your front line or disengage when you lack allied catch.

bad.note: Use a cheap Orb and attack range to contribute while recovering farm.

good.note: Add attack range and Yasha movement while the team can play slowly around you.

easy.note: Complete Pike early for positioning, then build toward Mage Slayer if you can keep landing hits on a spell threat.

swaps.note: Prioritize the spell-damage debuff when you can reach and keep hitting its source.
Complete Pike as your range and reposition purchase.
Get an attack window when repeated nonpiercing control stops you from applying poison.

plans.pickNote: Take Zeus when your team can protect a ranged caster and wants repeatable magical area damage. He can help check invisibility with Lightning Bolt vision.
watchFor: Low access to towers on his own

goodAgainst.note: Bolt vision can expose Riki in the relevant area. Keep detection and respect Smoke Screen.
Arc Lightning can pressure multiple nearby bodies when there is space to cast safely.

avoidAgainst.note: PA can jump into your casting range quickly. Position behind a teammate who can stop her.

bad.note: Keep mana flowing with Arcane Boots and add a range or save purchase to stay in fights.

good.note: Lean into spell output with Kaya and use Force to survive the first jump.

easy.note: Complete Scepter early for Nimbus map pressure, then add range or a utility item.

swaps.note: Prioritize safe positioning when enemy gap closers can reach you.
Buy a magic barrier for yourself or an ally when one burst window decides the fight.
Get a self-dispel and cyclone when a dispellable silence or telegraphed setup is the issue.

plans.pickNote: Mobile mid with split-map options. The draft needs reliable initiation if Ember must spend Remnants to disengage.

goodAgainst.note: Sleight can hit clustered copies. Its 80% Item Potency supports eligible lightning procs while Ember keeps his position.

avoidAgainst.note: Hex can stop a Remnant escape. Hold a safe angle until Lion shows.

bad.note: Use cheap Phase movement and Maelstrom to catch up on waves.

good.note: Buy Mage Slayer if you can apply its debuff to high-impact spellcasters, then secure a defensive timing.

easy.note: Complete Gleipnir quickly when holding targets improves your team’s follow-up damage.

swaps.note: Take debuff immunity before the next luxury purchase when you cannot use Remnant under control.
Get repeatable lightning for waves and copies at a reachable price.
Prioritize the debuff if you can hit the enemy spell source before it commits.

plans.pickNote: A mechanics-based flex option when the team needs mobile area disruption. Check the observed role count before treating it as part of the Legend sample.

goodAgainst.note: Diffusal pressure can matter before Wraith King has a mana-independent Reincarnation upgrade.

bad.note: Finish Diffusal and play around the mana-burn timing before saving for mobility.

good.note: Use a Blink first when reliable Rolling Thunder initiation matters more than damage.

easy.note: Complete Diffusal plus Blink early, then reserve the next major purchase for Scepter.

swaps.note: Consider Roll Up early if instant interruption blocks your setup.
Apply the spell-damage debuff when safe Swashbuckle hits can reach the enemy caster.
Bring Blink forward if targets can reliably play away from Rolling Thunder.

plans.pickNote: Pick Axe to punish opponents who must cluster or keep attacking in melee. Plan the Blink timing and confirm allied damage can finish the first Call.

goodAgainst.note: Call can hold a PA after she jumps without needing Axe to land normal attacks.
Call can catch clustered Chaos Knight illusions and expose the real hero to follow-up.
Area Call and spin pressure clustered copies. In 7.42, attacks that miss Axe also advance his Counter Helix counter.

bad.note: Keep boots cheap and finish Blink first so you can start fights while behind.

good.note: Add Phase armor and mobility, then choose your Blink angle before finishing Blade Mail.

easy.note: Get Phase, Blink and Blade Mail, then add Shard before the next major defensive purchase.

swaps.note: Protect teammates from repeated attack instances across a group. Its 7.42 active can be dispelled.
If the lineup needs an area magic barrier, buy it after the initiation timing.
Bring debuff immunity forward if enemy control stops you from getting the Call off.

plans.pickNote: A pickoff initiator with a dispel for allies. Check whether another hero covers waves and fights against multiple targets.

goodAgainst.note: An immediate Duel from fog can hold Storm for allied burst before he zips away.

avoidAgainst.note: Oracle can protect a Duel target. Catch Oracle or have someone interrupt the save.
A timely Shallow Grave can deny the Duel kill. Track Dazzle’s position.

bad.note: Get the initiation tool before the damage item if the team can follow up your Duel.

good.note: Buy Blade Mail first when it helps survive and contest the lane, then pair it with Blink.

easy.note: Use the extra farm to complete both tools and add Shard before the next big fight.

swaps.note: Protect the Duel entry against nonpiercing disruption before buying luxury damage.
Pressure the save caster with a silence when their dispels are scarce.
Take the early team barrier when nobody else can cover the magic burst.

plans.pickNote: Frontline and area initiation from a single pick. He works best with heroes that can use the Ravage window, including against tightly grouped opponents.

goodAgainst.note: Anchor Smash and area control help manage tightly grouped Chaos Knight illusions.
Time Ravage for the group and use Anchor Smash to pressure clustered bodies.

bad.note: Use basic boots and Blink plus a cheap sustain pickup to keep Ravage relevant.

good.note: Use team mana and Blink first, then buy the armor and sustain auras your team needs.

easy.note: Build Arcane and Blink, then reach Shiva's Guard for pressure on grouped attackers.

swaps.note: Choose an early group magic barrier when it lets allies survive the follow-up.
Prioritize damage block against repeated attacks from the zoo or a mass of copies.
Dispel a teammate and threaten reflection when spells are targeted. The original spell still resolves.

plans.pickNote: Draft Beastmaster when winning fights can lead to objectives. Check enemy wave clear and whether the team can make use of vision and auras.
watchFor: Teams that avoid the push and cut waves

goodAgainst.note: Roar can hold a mobile Storm for follow-up if you can start in range.

avoidAgainst.note: Do not group controlled units beside a valuable target for Sven’s cleave.

bad.note: Get an affordable team aura and hold an objective while recovering farm.

good.note: Buy Helm of the Dominator for controlled-unit utility, then secure a Roar setup.

easy.note: Reach Ristul's Devotion when you can group early, then add initiation and match-specific defense.

swaps.note: Shift the aura budget to a magic barrier if area damage is stopping the push.
Protect allies who are being hit by many enemy units; the active is dispellable.
Buy the Roar setup earlier when the enemy stays outside cast range.

plans.pickNote: Pick Rubick when the enemy reveals reliable spells worth stealing and your lane partner can trade. Prepare an escape route before stepping into steal range.

goodAgainst.note: If Tide uses Ravage and exposes it to Spell Steal, convert it into counter-initiation.
Reverse Polarity is high value if Magnus leaves it as a stealable last spell.

bad.note: Cheap boots and Pavise let you protect an ally while saving toward positioning.

good.note: Build Tranquils and Force to hold a safe steal angle and move allies away from danger.

easy.note: Complete Arcane Boots and Blink to contest fight positioning, then add cast range.

swaps.note: Buy a magic barrier when a single spell volley decides whether your core survives.
Buy the ally save earlier if positioning matters more than your own initiation.
Shield the ally drawing physical burst while holding a safe Spell Steal angle.
Prioritize dispel and reflection against targeted spells when the team can afford it.

plans.pickNote: Flexible ranged catch around trees and an option to pressure defensive passives with Sharpshooter. Check that your team has durable front-line vision.

goodAgainst.note: A landed Sharpshooter can start a Break window for the team’s burst.

avoidAgainst.note: Rage can interfere with a magic-control setup. Wait for your team to force it first.

bad.note: Complete Bloodslinger for a cheap ranged utility timing, then prioritise a save.

good.note: Add Force after Tranquils so your team can follow or escape the catch timing.

easy.note: When allies already cover saves, a Maelstrom timing can speed waves and add attack procs.

swaps.note: Use the early anti-heal slot if your lineup lacks a better Vessel carrier.
Buy the save ahead of damage when losing one ally loses the fight.
Move Force ahead of damage for teammates who need help escaping or getting into range.

plans.pickNote: Pick Spirit Breaker when early rotations can punish enemies spread across the map. Coordinate charge paths and avoid committing alone into defensive vision.

goodAgainst.note: Charge can create a response to a visible split-pusher if teammates can join safely.

avoidAgainst.note: Fast Hex or stun can interrupt arrival. Time your charge around Lion’s position.

bad.note: Use cheap movement for rotations, then buy affordable team utility.

good.note: Phase and an early Drum timing enable repeated group moves.

easy.note: Complete Phase and Blade Mail while ahead and shift toward protection if charges start feeding.

swaps.note: Shift rotation gold into anti-heal when kills depend on stopping a large recovery.
Buy protection before optional fight items if nonpiercing control interrupts the arrival.
Buy a reposition tool if your team needs help joining or leaving the engagement.

plans.pickNote: Draft Dazzle early if your team can supply initiation. Protect one key target and keep a position where the enemy has to commit twice to reach you.
watchFor: Enemies who jump the save caster

goodAgainst.note: A well-timed Shallow Grave can deny the Duel kill if you stay in cast range.

avoidAgainst.note: Culling Blade can finish a Grave target at its threshold. Use healing and repositioning before that point.

bad.note: Pavise provides a cheap physical save while your other gold covers support needs.

good.note: Buy Mekansm when team healing is the highest-impact first completed item.

easy.note: Use the larger budget for Tranquils and Force to cast and save from better positions.

swaps.note: Move the magic barrier ahead of healing when allies are dying before heals resolve.
Use an early physical barrier on the ally being focused before they fall into Grave range.
Bring Force forward when a teammate needs displacement to survive.
Coordinate one Vessel buyer if a large enemy heal is deciding fights.

plans.pickNote: Pick Lion for fast catch against mobile enemies. Make sure another teammate can cover lane and wave pressure if the team falls behind.

goodAgainst.note: Hex can stop Storm before an escape if you start within cast range.
An immediate disable can prevent Remnant escape during the kill attempt.

bad.note: Buy cheap boots and a first protection item before saving for Blink.

good.note: First Blink is feasible when you need to start fights against heroes who are otherwise too mobile.

easy.note: Finish Tranquils and Blink, then use the next purchase to improve cast range.

swaps.note: Add a save if counter-initiation is more important than starting the fight yourself.
Protect yourself against an attack-based jump if surviving to cast Hex decides fights.
Bring an ally reposition earlier if teammates die before you can counter-initiate.
Reach and Hex the save caster first so the team can commit its damage.

plans.pickNote: Draft Winter Wyvern to punish grouped physical attackers. Keep an eye on enemy magic damage before committing Cold Embrace.
watchFor: Burst magic on a Cold Embrace target

goodAgainst.note: Winter's Curse punishes a formation of high-damage units packed around a target.
Cold Embrace can cover an ally during a physical burst window if the enemy lacks follow-up magic.

avoidAgainst.note: Zeus can follow with magic through Cold Embrace. Favor a magic save when needed.

bad.note: Use cheap movement and Bloodslinger for small fight utility while saving a larger defensive item.

good.note: Finish Tranquils and Glimmer to layer a magic barrier over the physical save plan.

easy.note: Add Arcane and Blink quickly when your team can capitalize on your Curse positioning.

swaps.note: Buy magic protection early when Cold Embrace needs a second layer.
Use a physical barrier to protect someone who needs to keep moving and attacking.
Use an ally reposition to defeat enemy catch or preserve a safe Curse angle.
Choose the angle and timing to catch clustered units with Curse.
